en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yong of Baoning Monastery in Jinling:
When the old man of Mount Fengtai was traveling through the South, he arrived at the place where Yang Zhu wept at the forked road and encountered a spiritual friend.
With white snow covering his head, the Master sat in a lion’s posture. Using the golden circle and the thorny plum as his Buddhist teaching, he addressed the students of the ten directions, saying:
"The Iron Ring Mountains may be penetrated, but my Diamond Circle cannot be penetrated; the waters of the great ocean may be swallowed."

"I cannot swallow this *liji pong* (the thorn of the *vilva* fruit). If one can penetrate a single circle, then there will be no doubt in penetrating hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, and billions of circles;

all afflictions (*kleśa*) shall be liberated herein. If one can swallow a single *pong*, then there will be no doubt in swallowing hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, and billions of *pongs*;
all merits (*guṇa*) shall be accomplished herein. At that time, the bhikṣus were bewildered and withdrew from their seats. Do not...
As for that superior person who knows where to apply himself, he dwells with ease in the site of enlightenment and alone receives the prediction of his future buddhahood.

Fifteen years later, atop Mount Fengtai, a great thunderous sound resounds; the three types of grass and two types of trees are all equally moistened by a single rain. His disciples recorded these words.
I request that the Master Wúwéi compose a preface for this. Written on the Qingming Festival, the first year of the Yuánfēng era of the Huángsòng dynasty, by the Master Wúwéi, Yáng Jié.
Opening the Hall Preface.
Composed by Wang Zhi, Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, Palace Attendant,
Governor of the Military Prefecture, and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Regional Armies.

I humbly submit that the true wind of Western India and the secret seal of the Southern School— though a single word may lead to awakening to the Way— it still results in the distinction between medicine and disease.

"The three realms are mind-only. This distinguishes between the existence of form and emptiness. Yet, by employing metaphors as rafts to guide those at the first stage, one shatters the clouds of delusion and realizes the *pariniṣpanna-svabhāva* (the perfected nature).
Without relying on the transmission of a teacher, how could one reach the ultimate limit?
Thus, the Layman Vimalakīrti opened the gate of non-duality, and his kalaviṅka-like voice resonated throughout the great chiliocosm. Now, Master Yong of Chan is like a solitary cloud—refined and...
Furthermore: The bright moon’s pure form is like a flash of lightning struck by a swift trigger; the luster of the pearl is perfected through the observance of the precepts.
The four great elements are not the self, so they do not flow with the forms of green bamboos; the five aggregates are all empty, so how could one remain stuck in the knots of a flowered kerchief?

Now that the precious monastery has reached its term of vacancy, I respectfully entrust you with this mission to move [to this seat]. May you vibrate the sound of the tide and provide peace for the assembly of the ocean—within this lion throne.
Now, as the great drums resound, we gaze upon the ocean of compassion manifesting its sublime principles, so that all living beings may receive profound benefit.

The Sage’s wind blows with fervent vigor, and the ancestral legacy spreads its fragrance; thus this supreme condition is fulfilled, enduring imperishably through the ages. This brief memorial is respectfully submitted.
The Recorded Sayings of Venerable Master Yong of Baoning Chan Monastery,
compiled by his disciples (Dao-sheng and Yuan-jing),
and reprinted by the Kinsu Śramaṇa Tong-cheng.

Ascending the hall, after the introductory liturgy and the reading of the memorial have been completed, the Master points to the Dharma seat and says: "The Buddhas of the three periods and the ancestral masters of past and present are all here;
they have already turned the Great Wheel of Dharma and have passed away beneath the feet of everyone present. Do you see?
"Do you see? If you see, then the eyebrows and eyelashes are constantly emitting radiance. If you do not see, look! This mountain monk is now entering the mud and the water with every step.
Then the Venerable One offered incense, saying: "This single portion of incense is for the long life of the present Emperor.

We humbly pray that His Majesty may live ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years; that his imperial enterprise may equal the mountains and rivers, and his dynastic mandate be as enduring as the cauldron."
[He offers incense] across heaven and earth. Again, he holds up the incense: "This one portion of incense is offered for all the civil and military officials of the entire nation.

We humbly pray that their sagacious plans and strategies may be vast and far-reaching, and their meritorious achievements may flow on long and enduring. May the six armies always be at peace, and the myriad people forever secure. Again, he holds up the incense:
"O Great Assembly, this one portion of incense is priceless throughout past and present; it is not transmitted by Buddhas or patriarchs. Moreover..."
"The Way—where did you obtain it from? Do you still know its point of origin? If you do know, then right here you shall meet a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).
If you do not know, burn it in the incense burner as an offering to my late teacher, the Venerable Huihui, who first resided at Yangqi and later at Yungai.
Thereupon he ascended the seat. Jiangshan struck the gavel and said: "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should..."
Observing the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), the Master then looked at the assembly and said, "Do you understand thoroughly? If you do not understand thoroughly, it is like drawing legs on a snake.
Before the crags of the ancient Buddhas, a thousand blossoms compete in splendor; at the source of Caoxi, ten thousand streams converge in their flow.
Is there anyone here who can ascend these precipices and traverse this vast expanse? If you disregard danger and ruin, then I invite you to meet me. At that time, a monk asked:
In the past, at the single assembly on Vulture Peak, Kāśyapa heard it directly. On this day, the Prefect has graced the dais; I request the Master to raise the chant.
[The Master] replies: "The red sun is in the sky; the clear breeze pervades the earth. A monk says: "If one can blow the holeless flute, its sound is heard throughout the world.
[The Master] replies: "Hanshan claps his hands; Shide laughs 'he-he'. A monk says: "If one does not launch a boat, how can one know the vastness of the sea?"

[The Master] replied: "The movement for benefit is for the superior man. [The Questioner] asked: "I have heard the Prefect say that even 'awakening to the Way through a single word' still involves the discrepancy between medicine and illness.

Without relying on a single word, how does one receive people? [The Master] replied: "The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain and much wind. The monk said: [This is the end of the recorded exchange].

Carrying sun and moon upon a staff made of rabbit horns; pointing to heaven and earth with a whisk made of tortoise hair. [The Master] replies: "The ten directions, vertical and horizontal. The monk says:

"Incense smoke reaches far beyond the clear heavens; the morning canopy’s light descends to testify to the Patriarch’s mechanism. [The Master] replies: "Treading through straw sandals, running barefoot;
seeking a true friend within the land of Silla. [The Master] asks: "A skilled warrior does not employ a single blade. Today..."
[The Master said: "Right on the spot, how do you decide the victory? [The monk] replied: "Look! [The Master] said: "This is still meeting with weapons. [The monk] replied:

"The two parts are different. [The Master] said: "Untying the belt and laying down the arms is still a laborious effort; looking up to heaven and letting out a long whistle is not yet the achievement.

[The monk] replied: "One's acquaintances fill the world. [The Master] said: "If you suddenly encounter a mass of blades coming at you from all sides, what then? [The monk] replied: "I would take the beating."
"Not yet," [the Master] said. The monk said, "It would have been better to let it pass. The Master struck his knee once. The monk then gave a shout.
[The Master] replied, "A true adept. The monk hesitated. [The Master] replied, "This dullness will kill people. [The Master] asked, "In years past, those outside the clouds all understood;
what is the matter within the marketplace today? He replied, "This mountain monk loves anger and does not love joy. The monk said, "A brand-new sun and moon; a distinct heaven and earth."
[The Master] replied, "It is as if we had never met. The monk said, "On the side of Mount Ziling, a thousand flowers flourish; before the White Jade Tower, ten thousand people sing.
[The Master] replied, "It is not necessarily that what is in the heart matches what is in the mouth. The monk said, "A master of the school; you appeared in this world too late."
The Master replied, “This patch-robed monk is rare in the world. The monk said, “He is not even worth it. The Master let out a single sigh.
The monk asked, “When the Buddhas appeared in the world, the earth was strewn with golden lotuses. Now that you have appeared in the world, what auspicious signs are there?

The Master replied, “Blue sky and bright day. The monk said, “The five petals of fragrance transmit the precious seal; the Three Vehicles, once realized, transform humans and devas. The Master replied, “Cut it off!”
"Thousand Mountains Road. "Opening the Ten-Thousand-Li Pass. The monk said, "The golden breeze spreads afar; the village elders sing and chant. He replied, "In every place there are fragrant herbs.
The monk said, "If one does not board Xie Gong’s boat, how can one see the hand of the fisherman? He replied, "The heart bears no grudge against others; the face shows no shame.
One monk, having prostrated, knelt with his hands toward his chest and took something from within. He made a gesture...

The Master made a gesture of presenting something. The monk looked to the left. The Master stood up. The monk made a gesture of offering an object. The Master looked to the right. The monk reached out his hand as if to receive an object, then placed it back inside his robe. The Master pointed his hand straight down. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "There is only this; there is no 'that'. The monk made a sweeping motion with his hand in response. "Indeed," he said. The monk then returned to the assembly. The Master smiled and asked: [Question] "What is it? The monk remained silent. The Master struck him and said, "This fellow has not yet seen the Buddha-nature. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "If you had been able to see through this, you would have known that the Buddha-nature is not separate from your own face. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Do not mistake this for the Buddha-nature; the Buddha-nature is not like this. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-nature? The Master said, "It is precisely this very thing. The monk asked, "Is it not that which is beyond words and thought? The Master said, "If you speak of it, it is already not it. If you think of it, it is already not it. Do not seek it elsewhere; it is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one see it? The Master said, "If you try to see it, you will never see it. If you do not try to see it, you will see it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one hear it? The Master said, "If you try to hear it, you will never hear it. If you do not try to hear it, you will hear it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one know it? The Master said, "If you try to know it, you will never know it. If you do not try to know it, you will know it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one attain it? The Master said, "If you try to attain it, you will never attain it. If you do not try to attain it, you will attain it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one enter it? The Master said, "If you try to enter it, you will never enter it. If you do not try to enter it, you will enter it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one dwell in it? The Master said, "If you try to dwell in it, you will never dwell in it. If you do not try to dwell in it, you will dwell in it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one practice it? The Master said, "If you try to practice it, you will never practice it. If you do not try to practice it, you will practice it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one realize it? The Master said, "If you try to realize it, you will never realize it. If you do not try to realize it, you will realize it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one manifest it? The Master said, "If you try to manifest it, you will never manifest it. If you do not try to manifest it, you will manifest it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one benefit others? The Master said, "If you try to benefit others, you will never benefit them. If you do not try to benefit others, you will benefit them clearly. The monk asked, "How can one save sentient beings? The Master said, "If you try to save sentient beings, you will never save them. If you do not try to save sentient beings, you will save them clearly. The monk asked, "How can one turn the wheel of the Dharma? The Master said, "If you try to turn the wheel of the Dharma, you will never turn it. If you do not try to turn the wheel of the Dharma, you will turn it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one preach the Dharma? The Master said, "If you try to preach the Dharma, you will never preach it. If you do not try to preach the Dharma, you will preach it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one teach and transform? The Master said, "If you try to teach and transform, you will never teach or transform. If you do not try to teach and transform, you will teach and transform clearly. The monk asked, "How can one respond to circumstances? The Master said, "If you try to respond to circumstances, you will never respond. If you do not try to respond to circumstances, you will respond clearly. The monk asked, "How can one act spontaneously? The Master said, "If you try to act spontaneously, you will never act spontaneously. If you do not try to act spontaneously, you will act spontaneously clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be free from all attachments? The Master said, "If you try to be free from all attachments, you will never be free. If you do not try to be free from all attachments, you will be free clearly. The monk asked, "How can one transcend all dharmas? The Master said, "If you try to transcend all dharmas, you will never transcend them. If you do not try to transcend all dharmas, you will transcend them clearly. The monk asked, "How can one reach the ultimate source? The Master said, "If you try to reach the ultimate source, you will never reach it. If you do not try to reach the ultimate source, you will reach it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one attain the Way? The Master said, "If you try to attain the Way, you will never attain it. If you do not try to attain the Way, you will attain it clearly. The monk asked, "How can one become a Buddha? The Master said, "If you try to become a Buddha, you will never become one. If you do not try to become a Buddha, you will become one clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be liberated? The Master said, "If you try to be liberated, you will never be liberated. If you do not try to be liberated, you will be liberated clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be at peace? The Master said, "If you try to be at peace, you will never be at peace. If you do not try to be at peace, you will be at peace clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be joyful? The Master said, "If you try to be joyful, you will never be joyful. If you do not try to be joyful, you will be joyful clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be content? The Master said, "If you try to be content, you will never be content. If you do not try to be content, you will be content clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be satisfied? The Master said, "If you try to be satisfied, you will never be satisfied. If you do not try to be satisfied, you will be satisfied clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be fulfilled? The Master said, "If you try to be fulfilled, you will never be fulfilled. If you do not try to be fulfilled, you will be fulfilled clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be complete? The Master said, "If you try to be complete, you will never be complete. If you do not try to be complete, you will be complete clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be perfect? The Master said, "If you try to be perfect, you will never be perfect. If you do not try to be perfect, you will be perfect clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be whole? The Master said, "If you try to be whole, you will never be whole. If you do not try to be whole, you will be whole clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be integrated? The Master said, "If you try to be integrated, you will never be integrated. If you do not try to be integrated, you will be integrated clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be unified? The Master said, "If you try to be unified, you will never be unified. If you do not try to be unified, you will be unified clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be harmonious? The Master said, "If you try to be harmonious, you will never be harmonious. If you do not try to be harmonious, you will be harmonious clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be in accord? The Master said, "If you try to be in accord, you will never be in accord. If you do not try to be in accord, you will be in accord clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be in resonance? The Master said, "If you try to be in resonance, you will never be in resonance. If you do not try to be in resonance, you will be in resonance clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be in alignment? The Master said, "If you try to be in alignment, you will never be in alignment. If you do not try to be in alignment, you will be in alignment clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be in harmony with the Way? The Master said, "If you try to be in harmony with the Way, you will never be in harmony. If you do not try to be in harmony with the Way, you will be in harmony clearly. The monk asked, "How can one be in harmony with the D
The high officials of the court respectfully extended three invitations; eminent scholars and great masters all graced the occasion with their presence.

"I beg the Master to use his skillful means to point out the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West and to reveal the human mind. [The Master] replied: "The iron ox loves to eat rootless grass. The monk said:
"On this day, the moon’s orb shines with brilliance; everyone in the world sings songs of peace. [The Master] replied: "One who has no sinews in their eyes is poor for a lifetime."

The monk said, "The Dragon Diagram (Longtu) serves as witness; I, this student, prostrate in gratitude. [The Master] replied, "I let you off one move," and then said, "The question and answer are now complete;
why do you not disperse? Since that is not the case, I shall further draw out some more entanglements and create a scene of disorder upon the ground of purity.
The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye has persisted through all antiquity and the present; it has been secretly transmitted from patriarch to patriarch, seal after seal."
It is so. The path of language is cut off; thought and emotion are forgotten. All sentient beings possess this reality within themselves.
Yet, because it is a teaching difficult to believe, those who can apply it are rare. Only those of the highest capacity can truly settle into it.

Once one has settled therein, one participates equally with the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the three periods of time, and with all things, both animate and inanimate—there is nothing else. It is neither before nor after; it exists.
What birth-and-death is there to transcend? What Buddha-way is there to accomplish? Without depending on the cultivation of many kalpas, everything is fully perfected in the snap of a finger.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, one acts spontaneously; seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing, one applies oneself according to conditions.
When sleep comes, the eyes close; when food comes, the mouth opens. In the cold, one turns toward the fire; in the heat, one seeks coolness. Having arrived at this field of plain reality—

The ground is insufficient above and excessive below. If you are a guest at the gate of the ancestral patriarchs, you must hide your body within the flames and gallop your horse through a mote of dust;

surging eastward and sinking westward, dying together and living together, such that the *śakrāksa* eye cannot peer into it and the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot grasp it. You must shatter the seal of Vairocana and sweep away all monks.
[This is] the trace. Yet, although it is thus, the road of Jian Gate is perilous yet ultimately easy to cross; the pass of Zhaozhou is treacherous and exceedingly difficult to traverse.

However, I, Renyong, am by nature dull-witted and have long been of little learning. Though I have drawn upon the pivot of the ancestral school, I intended to remain deep within the thicket [of seclusion].

Recently, I received the command from the Knowledge-Governor, the Dragon Diagram Official (Longtu), graciously bestowing his imperial mandate. The officials and staff of the entire administration likewise granted their unanimous approval, ordering me to follow this [duty] henceforth.

At this site of enlightenment, I am truly honored by this great fortune. I venture to invoke the highest goodness to look upward for Your Majesty’s long life and to offer prayers on behalf of the officials of the administration.

I humbly pray that the Lord Prefect, Dragon Diagram (Longtu), may soon ascend to the imperial court and attain the honor of the Grand Council (Dinghuai); and that the Commissioner of Transport, Minister of Personnel (Langzhong), may swiftly achieve the highest distinction in his grain transport duties.

Having been exceptionally favored by imperial grace, you were appointed as a Judge of the Department of Transport (Dugu). Your illustrious reputation has spread afar, and you have rapidly ascended to a pure office.

Serving as a Vice Commissioner of the Department of Carriages, your conduct among the officials of the entire administration has further illuminated your character. You have made a swift advance upon the broad path of success.

We pray that at this present banquet, you—distinguished official of the outer ministry—may forever remain a trusted confidant of the royal house and always enjoy the profound favor of the Buddha’s treasure. Furthermore, we receive [the greetings of] the Master of the Monastic Office.
Master Qingliang of Mount Jiangshan has graciously lent his presence to join us in establishing this Dharma assembly.

May all patrons ever attain blessings and prosperity, and forever adorn the Buddha Vehicle. He then said: "The Great Transformation is effortless; the Way is at peace. The sun and moon over Jambudvīpa shine ever more clearly.
In years of plenty, the village elders sing with joy; Everywhere, auspicious grain grows with ears joined together. [He sat] for a long time.
"Venerable officials, I humbly pray that you take care of yourselves.

While the Master was at Jiangshan receiving the minor ordination, the great assembly had gathered in formation. A monk presented a Dharma robe, and the Master picked up the *kāṣāya* he was wearing himself and said:
'Great assembly, tell me: which one is this, and which one is that? If you say this one is it, how can you account for...'"
"What about that one? If you say 'that one' is it, what about 'this one'? He then looked at the assembly and said, "Now, I cannot help but change my head and face before this great assembly;
I shall grasp and let go, and come and go. Thereupon, he removed his *kāṣāya* robe and donned his dharma robes, ascended the seat, and said:
"The wind does not blow, the forest does not move; going downhill, one does not run—such a swift opportunity is rarely encountered."
At that time, a monk asked, "Under the walls of the city of Jinling, the Patriarch’s command is being put into practice.
What is the Patriarch’s command being put into practice? The Master said, "A flash of lightning has long appeared within the clouds; a sudden peal of thunder has now resounded for many moments.

The monk pressed further, "The light of the lunar orb shines upon this very day. The Master replied, "It reveals one's liver and gallbladder. The monk continued, "Do not say that King Liang did not recognize Bodhidharma."

[The Master] grinds [the inkstone]. He answers: "When the time comes, heaven and earth all exert their power together. [The student] asks: "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they turn the Great Dharma Wheel.

Now that you, Master, have appeared in the world, what auspicious signs are there? He answers: "The mountains are green and the waters are blue. The student advances, saying: "I, this student, do not yet understand. I beg the Master to point it out again. He answers:
"A gust of wind comes, and with it a chill. The student advances, saying: "An equal-toned stringless lute—only the Master can play it."
"Excellent. [The Master] replied, "For now, do not call a bell a jar. [The Disciple] asked, "I do not ask about dwelling long in mountain valleys;

how is it regarding entering the marketplace to transform and guide? [The Master] replied, "The true does not conceal the false. [The Disciple] pressed further, saying, "If that is so, then all living beings will have someone to rely upon.

[The Master] replied, "Curves and straightness are clearly distinguished. [The Disciple] said, "All living beings have already received the Teacher’s instruction. As for the matter of the Supreme Vehicle (the *zongcheng*):"
"What? He replied, "A person's spring resides on the highest peak. Jìn said, "The four seas together study the true Prajñā;
the ten directions equally employ the Buddha’s Vinaya. He replied, "Thirty years hence, before those with clear eyes, you must not speak erroneously. The monk said:
The Prefect did not falsely extend his request for life; the student prostrated himself to thank the Master’s kindness.

[The Master] replied: “Keep this clearly in mind. A monk asked: “When the Buddhas appear in the world, the earth is spread with gold. When a human king appears in the world, he benefits people through his grace.

When you, Master, appear in the world, with what do you instruct people? [The Master] replied: “The northern and southern mountains face each other; east and west, there are paths that divide. The monk said: “Zhongfu [Mountain]...”

Auspicious vapors arise before the peaks; beside the Phoenix Terrace, the ancestral wind flourishes. [The Master] replies: "How many sightseers and pleasure-seekers reach this place and yet remain utterly lost to the source?
The monk says: "The chrysanthemum turns its face toward the sun; the passing waters flow on without returning. [The Master] replies:

"Vaguely it resembles a melody, just barely fit to be heard, yet it is blown away once more into another tune. The monk steps forward and says: "May the assembly bear witness; I, this student, prostrate in thanks."
[The student] replied, "When prostrating, one must simply touch the head to the ground. The Master said, "Are there no others who wish to ask questions?
What harm is there in coming forward to form a karmic connection? The Master then said, "Those who study the Way must possess the eye atop the crown of their heads.

As transcendent heroes, they shall thunder the Dharma-thunder and beat the Dharma-drum before all the multitudes of devas and humans; they shall conceal the point while revealing the blade, and seize the drumstick."
Seizing the banner, roaring the lion’s roar, and performing the great work of the Buddha—if one can do so, only then does one possess even a fraction of the spirit of a true man.
Today, this mountain monk, not sparing a single hair on his brow, shall enter the mud and the water. My Buddha, the World-Honored One...
“It is for the sake of one great matter that I have appeared in the world. I venture to ask the virtuous ones: what is this one great matter? After a long silence, he said:
“The five thousand-plus volumes cannot fully explain it; the Buddhas of the three periods cannot praise it enough;
the patriarchs of past and present cannot lift it up. Do you understand? If you do understand, without moving a step, you transcend Śākyamuni.”
Passing over Maitreya, why must I, this mountain monk, further beat my two pieces of skin before you virtuous ones, degrading the noble to the base?
Nevertheless, though it be so, "not permitting night travel, one must firmly hold a torch; one must simply show oneself to others on the road."
He then said: "The furnace, bellows, tongs, and hammer have labored in vain; why must a blade as sharp as a hair be ground?
Last night, the numinous light shone upon the Ox and Dipper constellations, bringing peace and prosperity throughout the universe. He stood for a long while.

On the day of conferring the certificate, the Master ascended the seat and said, "Is there anyone who would like to ask a question? A monk stepped forward. The Master said, "Casually casting the line.
After the monk had prostrated, he drew a circle. The Master tossed it behind him with his right hand.
The monk drew another circle, and the Master tossed it behind him with his left hand. The monk returned to the assembly. The Master asked, "What else is there? The monk was silent.

[The Master] spoke. He struck his knee and said, "A dragon’s head with a snake’s tail. The monk said, "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled. The Master laughed and continued, "A bright pearl passes through the palm;
those who discern it are rare. A precious mirror stands upon its stand; who can gaze into its reflection? On the single path before the blade, all idle talk is cut off.
Below, amidst a thousand differences, one follows the waves and drifts with the current. Therefore, when it is unfolded, the great chiliocosm is all [encompassed]."
"Pervasive. If it were not unfolded, not even a hair's breadth would remain. Such talk is still the teaching of the gate of transformation (*nirmāṇa*). But tell me:

how do you speak that phrase which does not fall into the gate of transformation? "The Way being secure, the Emperor’s decree is not transmitted; the times being peaceful, one need not sing the Song of Great Peace.
After the formal thanks, he said: "A thousand peaks stand like walls, slippery as moss; I spare no effort to expose my eyebrows."
"Come forth! Right here, you have already traveled more than ten million miles; how could you possibly linger any longer? With a shout, he descended from his seat.

When the Master entered the monastery, he was welcomed to the front of the Dharma Hall, whereupon he pointed to the seat and said: "O Great Assembly! Sublime and majestic, encompassing all phenomena."
Difficult to conceal; it penetrates from above through below. Who dares to take this up? He then ascended the seat and said, "One, two, three.

As soon as he was seated, he looked at the assembly and asked, "Do you understand thoroughly? If you do not understand thoroughly, I shall scatter sand and scatter earth! [This was under] the gate of Kāśyapa.
Not a drop can leak through. Before a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, the paths of both ordinary beings and sages are cut off.
Now tell me: is it to hold fast, or is it to let go? When the law is fully applied, there are no subjects left. If you have doubts, ask away. (The question and answer are not recorded. He then said:
"If you wish to ascend this seat, you must first pay homage to Sumeru-dīpa-rāja. Now tell me, where is Sumeru-dīpa-rāja? And where do you go to pay homage?"
Regarding the Rites: Is it that the mind dwells upon thoughts and intentions? Or is it that both objective conditions and mental deliberations are forgotten?

Or is it that the mind and its objects are one and the same? Or is it that all phenomena are empty and still? If you hold such views, you have not yet emerged from the common flow. Since it is not like this, then how is it?
"A staff strikes the head of a stone man; *bò bò*, he speaks of the actual reality. Even if one possesses vast learning and powerful memory, or worldly wisdom—
Discerning and eloquent, he attained great *dhāraṇī* and possessed unimpeded eloquence. Yet, under the gate of the Patriarch, he turned away from all engagement.
Thus, this matter cannot be sought with a mind of intentionality, nor can it be attained by a mind of non-intentionality;

it cannot be constructed through speech, nor can it be communicated through silent stillness. It is neither gain nor loss, neither right nor wrong, neither monastic nor lay, neither noble nor base, and it transcends the distinctions between ordinary beings and sages.
This is within the reach of those whose capacity for discernment and wisdom is sufficient. When people arrive here, how can they be said to have "arrived"?
If one is a true man of great character, then directly beneath this, truth cannot be obscured by falsehood. At the most intimate point, one must personally consent before it becomes intimate.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, I have already buried [the matter] myself. Is there anyone present now who will not be deceived? Excellent!
Jiuyun said, "Throughout my life, I have laid open my liver and gall toward others; though we know one another, it is as if we do not.
He then took up his staff and said, "Countless clouds and mountains cannot conceal it; yet he carries his cane-staff into the marketplace.
Beating at a thousand doors and ten thousand households, today he clearly plants his staff upon the Phoenix Terrace. With a single strike, he descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, he struck the meditation seat and said: "Outside the mind there are no dharmas; the myriad dharmas are but the mind. Since the mind does not arise, from where could dharmas be established?
Where did the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come from? Thirty years hence, if someone should ask you about the 'turning-the-body phrase,' how will you answer?
After a long silence, he said: "The Tong Pass is easy to cross, but the Sword Gate is all the more difficult to traverse. *Chan*.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The inexhaustible ocean of all dharma-gates is gathered together within this single site of the Way.
Picking up his staff, he said: 'O staff! When it meets with cold, the whole world is cold; when it meets with heat, the whole world is hot.
But tell me, how do you speak that phrase which is neither cold nor hot? He struck the meditation seat once and said: 'Next year there will surely be many new branches.'"
The spring wind continues to disturb all without ceasing.

*Chan* (Examine). Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "The moon appears in a thousand rivers; ten thousand streams flow back to their source. The long pole with its straight hook catches the great turtle.
The myriad phenomena of the forest and the heavens are all contained herein. Now I am selling this cheaply to you all—do you still want it?"
"If you want it, what can it do for you? If you do not want it, let it go forth into the great ocean to raise clouds and bring rain, to stir up winds and create waves.
He struck the meditation platform once, then gave a shout and descended from his seat.

Question: Whose song does the Master sing? To whom does his lineage of the school’s wind (zongfeng) succeed? Answer: When walking until the water ends, sit and watch the clouds arise. [The questioner] advances, saying:
You are the true son of Yangqi and the descendant of Linji. Answer: A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them.
Furthermore: "A swallow chasing after a stream flies over a low wall. Question: "What is the Buddha? Answer: "The one nearest the fire is scorched first. Question: "What is the Way? Answer:
"Sinking into mud, there are thorns. He pressed further: "What is it like for one on the Way? Answer: "One must strictly avoid treading upon it."
He then said: "The mind turns according to the myriad objects; where it turns, it is truly profound. If you recognize your nature as it flows along, there is neither joy nor sorrow.
He struck the meditation seat and said: "Baoning is going off to become a water buffalo.
Is there anyone who will follow me? If you can follow, where is your nose-ring? If you cannot follow, Baoning shall go off by himself."
He turned and left. He spoke again: "When there is spirit, add more spirit; where there is no elegance, there too is elegance. Ascending the hall, he said:
"If a single dharma has form, it obscures your eyes. When the eyes are not clear, the world appears jagged and vast.
Holding up his staff, he asked, "Do you see it? If you see it, you block your own vision; if you do not see it, you lose the staff. Now, what will you do?"
"How is it? [The Master asked. "Speak the phrase that does not allow oneself to be deceived. After a long silence, he said: "Level ground is not yet considered perilous;
how could distant mountains suffice as high? He struck his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Time passes in an instant; cold and heat alternate in succession. Without waiting for the conditions of spring, bring me a phrase of the Way.
After a long silence, he said: "I first saw it on the ninth day of the ninth month last year; this year I see the autumn leaves yellow again. *Chan*.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Since I first took up residence at Baoning, I have never been idle; day after day I walk the streets and alleys.
When I encounter Zhang San or Li Si, I raise my eyebrows—what do you say to that? He clapped his hands and laughed, then descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he struck the meditation seat and said, "It is not the mind, nor is it the Buddha. I ask you: what, after all, is this?
Last night, Vajra opened his eyes wide in rage; with a single blow, he shattered the cave of the vital spirit. He let out a shout and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: My mouth is full of tongues, yet none can speak it. The old barbarian with blue eyes has missing teeth at his gate.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall and cites the travels of Danxia. Upon arriving at a monastery during a cold snap, Danxia took a wooden Buddha and threw it into the fire.
The head monk of the monastery rebuked and cursed him, whereupon the head monk’s eyebrows and beard fell off. Great assembly, [the head monk’s] eyebrows...
His beard fell off. Let us set that aside for now. But tell me: are Danxia’s eyebrows still there?
If you can see this, you are a fellow student of the ancient Buddhas; if you do not see it, you must take care not to deny cause and effect.

Later, a monk asked Tianzhu, "What was the meaning of Danxia burning the wooden Buddha? Tianzhu said, "When cold, one huddles around the hearth toward the warm fire; when hot, [one seeks] the bamboo."
Sitting by a forest stream, Baoning said, "I have no wooden Buddha for you all to burn; within this hall there is naturally no smoke or fire.
If you wish to approach it, you may approach; if you wish to poke at it, you may poke. Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different? He then said:
In the upper hall there are many monks; in the lower hall there are few monks.
Entering the hall, [the Master] said: "When one person gives rise to the true and returns to the source, the voids of the ten directions all vanish away. He struck the meditation seat and said:
"Great assembly, why is it that some people still fail to pass through this? After a long silence, he said: "From now on I shall not return;
were I to return, I would surely find it. Who else could vie for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "A swift horse requires but one lash; a swift man requires but one word. Even if you are thus, you are still but a dull-witted fellow.
He then called to the assembly, saying, "Go drink tea."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Śākyamuni shut his room in Magadha, yet he already leaked the celestial mechanism. Vimalakīrti remained silent in Vaiśālī, yet he spoke all the more.
At Shaolin, for nine years he faced the wall; even in old age, he would not let his mind rest. At Caoxi, Yongjia stayed for only one night."
Vainly boasting of one's own brilliance and talent. Baoning, do you have any fault in saying this? "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one presents one's sword;
if not a poet, one does not offer a poem. *Chan*.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When a single mote of dust enters right concentration, all motes arise in samādhi; when all motes enter right concentration, a single mote arises in samādhi.
He then took up his staff and said: "Baoning sometimes takes the head to make the tail, and sometimes takes the tail to make the head."

The soles of the Vajra-feet stumble and leap; one hides the body within the eyes of a gnat. Reaching the Western Heaven in the morning and returning to the Eastern Land in the evening—let that be set aside for now.
But as for this single phrase, "Without moving a step," how would you speak of it? (He plants his staff on the ground and says:
"If there is nothing to do, do not travel by devious paths; otherwise, you will casually provoke the arrival of strife. *Chan*.
Question: What is the Buddha? Answer: An iron hammer with no hole. Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Answer: Frost added to snow.

Master Fahua ascended the hall and said: "The entire world of the ten directions constitutes a single great battle array. Whether saint or ordinary person, no matter what kind of being they may be, none can escape this.
Śākyamuni is the commander-in-chief, Mañjuśrī is the vanguard, and Samantabhadra is the rearguard.
Now that the formation is complete, tell me: with whom do you meet? After a long silence, he said: 'Dingguang is far away in Jindi.'"
He beckoned with his hand. The Wise One (Zhizhe) nodded his head in the dark at Jiangling. [Baoning] then took up his staff and said: "Now all are present upon the tip of Baoning’s staff.
The gate of ambrosia is opened; the true mark is revealed. Expansion and contraction are unimpeded; movement in any direction is free."
Do you see? If you see it, truth does not conceal falsehood.

If you do not see it, I entrust it to the masters who travel to all quarters, to take it as they please to southern provinces or northern counties—to help it cross the waters of the broken bridge and accompany it back to the moonless village.
(He strikes once and descends from his seat.)

Ascending the hall on the Day of the Start of Spring, [the Master] beats the clay oxen—one blow, two blows; a thousand heads, a hundred heads. Deeply covered by falling snow, they cannot be distinguished.
Those with eyes upon the crown of their heads merely wander in vain. Clapping his hands, he says: "Lalala!
The spring wind, though vexed, has not yet ceased."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are but the awakening of the nature. Fundamentally, there is no person who is deluded or enlightened;
it simply requires that you realize it this very day. But tell me, what is this matter of realization? After a long pause, he said: "When the snow has melted away, spring will naturally arrive."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The golden-maned lion lets out a single roar, startling the Dharma-body into rising from its storehouse beneath the Northern Dipper.
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have nowhere to run; even the blue-eyed one merely boasts of his skillful hand. He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: Kāśyapa raised his fists; Ānanda joined his palms; Ruci Tathāgata had no skill at all.
At the Guangfu Monastery in Changzhou, the Master ascended the hall: "In a lion’s den, there can be no other beasts. Is there anyone here who can roar?"

A monk asked: "Having traveled far from the hall of Jinling, you have fortunately arrived at this Guangfu monastery. Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school, we pray that the Master will proclaim it.
The Master replied: "A gentle breeze stirs the precious bells; the crimson sun shines upon the azure sky. The monk pressed further:

"The mountain scenery fills the eyes with its elegance; wild flowers everywhere are fresh and new. The Master replied: "White clouds stretch for a thousand miles, then ten thousand. The monk said: "May the assembly bear witness to this learning."

The people bowed in thanks. He replied: "It has been many years. Today, I cannot help but comply with human sentiment and offer some long-standing, unrotting vines of entanglement as an offering to the great assembly. Thus it is in every atom, thus it is in every world-system:
the mountains are mountains and the waters are waters. Maitreya does not enter the pavilion; Sudhana need not snap his fingers."
With a single stroke of his hand, he said: "The world-systems of fine dust melt away like ice and crumble like tiles. Now tell me, where are Maitreya and Sudhana?
If you can penetrate this point here, you will undoubtedly be honored wherever you go.
If you do not see it, the traveler's road is as vast as the sky, and the gates of the nobles are as deep as the sea.

Returning to the monastery, he ascended the hall and said: "I recall that one day after the purification ceremony, Master Guoshan did not go to the hall, but instead went into the abbot’s quarters to sleep.
After the midday meal, an administrator came and said, 'Why has the Master not gone to the hall? Guoshan replied:"
In the morning, he ate oil-cakes at the manor. In the evening, the manor master arrived and said, "Today I thank the Master for eating my oil-cakes.
"The assembly, is this the Master’s wondrous functioning? Is his fundamental nature simply like this? On level ground, he deliberately acts strangely."
Since it is not so, then how is it? After a long silence, he said: "This koan is left entirely to the judgment of all people under heaven.
Baoning possesses neither supernatural powers nor wondrous functions; I have no knowledge of past lives or the minds of others.
The monastery is in Jiangning Prefecture, while the estate belongs to Yixing County. By waterway it is a thousand *li*, by land four hundred. There are solitary boats and wild ferries everywhere."
Passing by the willows by the embankment and the flowers on the rocks, they bloom in leisure from time to time. I went out last month and returned yesterday;

at the manor, we never ate oil-cakes, but simply steamed white rice and boiled wild vegetable soup to satisfy our hunger and fill our bellies, according to the family’s means, whether abundant or meager.
Even so, there is yet another matter worthy of laughter: every single grain within that rice...
"Everywhere there are insects. [Pause. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Entering a weedy field, one does not pick; one simply takes whatever grass comes to hand. It is never absent from what meets the eye—why do you not speak when the moment arrives?
He then continued: "Today, Baoning exerts himself for the sake of the assembly; I am entering the weedy field! [He held up his staff.]
It is said: "Sometimes it grows with the spring; sometimes it does not flourish with the summer. It can kill people, and it can also bring people to life. To kill people:
the supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) turns into a lethal poison. To bring people to life: all lethal poisons are nothing but *amṛta*.
Now, I shall no longer conceal it in a bag; I will clearly display it before everyone. Tell me: is this *amṛta*?"
"This is poison. After a long pause, he said, "Do not take it lightly when there is no need; how many people have been misled by it throughout past and present?
He struck once and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall: This is the ancient capital of Jinling, a precious site upon the Phoenix Terrace. Here, all you people of supreme goodness have gathered in one place.
Disregarding the bequeathed teachings of Śākyamuni and awaiting no prediction from Maitreya, let spring pass and autumn come as they may; it matters not to us whether salt is cheap.

"Rice is expensive. At the two meal times, he spreads his bowl and opens his mat, speaking of rare delicacies and a hundred flavors; when energetic, he practices walking meditation, and when weary, he sleeps.
One hears only of the elephant king’s trampling—how could one know he has attained the lion’s play? He struck the meditation seat and said:
"Great assembly! Today at the fifth watch, the Water-Buffalo of Mount Gui has lost his nostrils.

He descends from his seat. Entering the hall, he holds his staff horizontally and says: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. Licorice is sweet; yellow-root is bitter. The vast waves surge, flooding the heavens;
atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, the sun is at its zenith. He strikes the ground with his staff and descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Tathāgata attained enlightenment at the appearance of the morning star. Tell me, assembly, when does the morning star not appear?
He ascended the hall, remained silent for a long while, then slapped his own mouth and said: "How many mouths have you grown?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "It is like the lute, the harp, the *konghou*, or the *pipa*: though they possess exquisite sounds, if there are no skillful fingers, they can never produce them.
Holding up his staff, he said: "This here is neither lute nor harp, yet it has a great, wondrous sound.
Is there anyone among you who possesses skillful fingers? Please try to bring it forth for us. If there is no one, Baoning will play it himself."

Holding his staff horizontally, he asked, "Do you hear it? After a long silence, he said, "The wind is cold and still throughout the hall; the meaning of a thousand ages is clearly manifest. Ascending the hall, he said:
"On the road to Caoxi, the rustic old man sings and chants; before the ancient Buddha hall, the traveler twirls his sleeves. With feet planted firmly on the ground, all people in the world know it.
But as for the nostrils reaching up to the heavens—how can one discern them? He then said, "It is like blowing a flute with no holes."
*Yunwai Qu* (Song of Beyond the Clouds): "Where in the Five Lakes can one find a true知音 (zhīyīn—'one who knows the sound')?
The Abbot of Changlu came, and [the Master] ascended the hall. Gold is tested by fire; water is tested by the staff.
"Great assembly, what if gold were not tested by fire, and water were not tested by the staff? Is there anyone here who can discern this? If you can discern it, then it is..."
Real or false? Deep or shallow? If you cannot discern this, then entrust it to those with clear eyes.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A seamless whole is truly difficult to swallow; broken into pieces, it cannot be fished out. To transform the raw into the cooked requires the person themselves.
When the five flavors are harmonized, they all return to the mouths of the multitude. Setting aside the multitude’s mouths for a moment..."
The Way. Who is the person who truly embodies it? If you can recognize him, he is the one on the long bed, spreading out his mat and unfolding his bowl.
If you do not know him, do not let us deceive one another after thirty years have passed. *Can*.
Question: I have heard it said of old: "Detached from form, detached from name, people do not recognize him; having used the 'blow-off-the-hair' sword, he must quickly polish it again.
[The Master] makes a gesture with his hand and says, "I do not ask about this; how is it used? Answer: "The King’s law knows no favoritism. The monk then bows. The Master strikes him.
The monk says, "The General already possesses a glorious reputation. Answer: "The ice melts and the tiles shatter."
Ascending the hall, he said: "With a head but no horns; with a tail but no feet. Where in the worlds of the ten directions can it be placed?
The golden crow comes every day to scorch and melt it away; even the jade hare is swallowed by him. He let out a long sigh and descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example: "Emptiness can be emptied, yet it is not true emptiness; form can be formed, yet it is not true form. True form has no shape; true emptiness has no name.
No-name is the father of names; no-form is the mother of forms. It is the root-source of all dharmas and the primordial ancestor of heaven and earth. The Master said:
"Dharma Master Sengzhao exerted every ounce of his strength, yet he did not even manage to say half of it."
Why is this? If one has attained the "Eye" beneath the gate of Makhadeva, one has not yet even dreamed of it beneath the gate of the Patriarch.
Tell me, what is the distinct excellence found beneath the gate of the Patriarch? It is said: "Do not raise it before those with wisdom;
do not speak of it before those without wisdom."
Ascending the hall: At dawn there is congee; at the time of the midday meal there is rice. Spreading the bowl and opening the sitting mat, the radiance is brilliantly clear.
Walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—there is nothing else; the great task of a lifetime is accomplished. The assembly, tell me: what of such a person’s understanding?
"Is it truly perfect yet? After a long silence, he said: "Who knows there is yet another traveler leaving home? Gazing toward the distant clouds, a deep sorrow arises.
He ascended the hall and said: "Baoning has a single path; east and west are merely pointers. Even looking straight down, there are already a thousand divergences; turning one's head back..."
A mistake? No mistake. At the top of a hundred-foot pole, one must advance further. Looking at the assembly, he said:
"Ahead there is both mountain and water; one journey is divided into two."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The autumn wind is cool; the pine tones are long. The traveler who has not yet returned thinks of his native land. But tell me: who is this traveler who has not yet returned?
Where is that native land? After a long silence, he said: "Upon the long continuous bed, there is porridge."
On account of a donor ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The thunderous voice has already resounded throughout the sands of the world;

now that we have met today, what is the matter? He replied: "Long rains have not ceased. The monk said: "If so, it is like adding flowers to brocade. He replied: "It steams the heavens and scorches the earth."
The monk said, "Please rise, Master. The Master then struck him and said, "Since the question was inexhaustible, the answer was likewise infinite.
According to the tradition of our ancestors, there is fundamentally no such thing; yet within the gate of transformative teaching, one provides expedients according to the occasion."
"How great it is! Yongjia said: 'Alas for the Dharma of the Final Age, in this degenerate era; sentient beings have meager merit and are difficult to discipline.
Far removed from the Sage, false views run deep; demons are strong and the Dharma weak, with much resentment and harm.
Yongjia spoke thus merely to temporarily accommodate human sentiments. However, even so, after a thousand ages, he must still be subjected to critical scrutiny."
Why is this? Furthermore, in my own house there has never been such a thing. No Buddhas have ever appeared in the world;

there is no Buddha to be realized, no Dharma to be taught, no sentient beings to be delivered, no afflictions to be severed, no enlightenment to be sought, and no nirvana to be realized. There is no beginning, middle, or end; nor is there any...
In the periods of the True Dharma, the Semblance Dharma, and the Final Dharma, when one seeks the actual nature within all phenomena, it is entirely unattainable.
Why is this? Because time neither comes nor goes, and phenomena neither arise nor perish. One does not perceive a path; all phenomena are unborn, and all phenomena are undestroyed.
If one can understand in this way, the Buddhas are ever manifest before one. Thus, Changsha said: "Exhausting the ten..."
The ten directions of the world are this śramaṇa’s single eye; the entirety of the ten directions of the world is this śramaṇa’s whole body.
The entirety of the ten directions of the world is this true human body; the entirety of the ten directions of the world is the gate of liberation.
Even Buddhas and sentient beings, the animate and the inanimate, those with nature and those without nature—all are of one and the same substance, of one and the same nature.
It is of a single characteristic, and likewise possesses no interior, exterior, or middle.

It is free from grasping and rejecting, love and hatred, annihilationism and eternalism, arising and ceasing, defilement and purity, coming and going—all such conceptualizations of various forms of knowledge and understanding. If one can be thus, then the three realms cannot contain them, nor can the six paths encompass them.
Everywhere they employ movement and coming and going, dwelling nowhere and clinging to nothing, manifesting forms in response to things.
They attain great mastery; whether ordinary or holy, right or wrong, acting contrary to or in accordance with the flow—Heaven cannot fathom them.
Thus, when Yongjia arrived here, he could not bring forth his hand. Furthermore, I recall Benjing saying: "The essence of the Way is fundamentally without cultivation;
without cultivating, one naturally accords with the Way. To cast aside the single true nature and enter into this vast clamor—if you encounter cultivation..."
O practitioner of the Way: first, do not speak of "the Way. This is truly what is meant by words of sincerity and honesty; Bao Ning maintains this very principle.
For now, let us adapt to circumstances and achieve perfection. Nevertheless, though it is thus, those who laugh at me are many, while those who admire me are few.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The sound of the wind roars on; Avalokiteśvara expounds the Dharma-gate of non-duality. The spring colors linger; Vairocana manifests the realm of formlessness.
Geese return to the sandy passes; orioles warble in the lofty trees. White crane-like clouds drift across the vast sky; rain like falling fat sprinkles the great fields.
Truly, it may be said that every point is radiant and every place is illuminated. Holding up his staff, he said:
Throughout the three periods of time and the ten directions, nothing exists apart from this very place. He lets out a single breath and says: "The eyelashes and eyebrows have all fallen away;
I know not on what day they shall grow back again."
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Sansheng, saying: "When I meet a person, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others.

Xinghua said: "When I meet a person, I do not come forth; when I come forth, I immediately act for the sake of others. These two venerable masters acted for the sake of others in such a way that they still remained halfway there.
Today, Baoning, seeing injustice on the road, takes up his staff and descends from his seat; the assembly all run away at once.
He scattered [the flowers], threw them away, and returned to his quarters.
He ascended the hall and said: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya; beneath the earth there is no Maitreya.
Having shattered the great void, how can one fail to find him? He lowered one foot and said: "O Great Assembly, where has he gone?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Śākyamuni appeared in the world, playing with the false as if it were real. Bodhidharma came from the West, taking the long and making it short.
Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout are like a mirage used to satisfy hunger or a plum tree used to quench thirst. In a world of purity and peace, there is no hindrance to traveling by night."
Is there anyone here now who can swallow up the Buddhas and patriarchs and shatter the illusory city? After a long silence, he said:
"Today, Baoning has been thoroughly exposed by the great assembly."
Ascending the hall, he said: "For over twenty years, this mountain monk has carried his sack and bowl across the seas to visit some dozen or so spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
Yet, within myself, I have had no place of realization; I am like a block of dull stone.

As for the venerable masters I studied under, they too had no superior qualities by which I might have been benefited. Since then, for the rest of my life, I have done nothing but remain one who understands nothing at all."
This fellow was originally quite pitiable. Suddenly, blown by the winds of karma, he arrived at Jiangning Prefecture.
Without cause, he was made to ascend the hall and pushed to the crossroads, where he took up residence in a dilapidated monastery as a master of gruel and rice, receiving guests from all directions.
Having no choice in the matter, he provided salt and vinegar according to his means; with gruel and rice sufficient for all, he simply passes the time in this manner.
"If this were the Buddha-dharma, I would not have dreamed of it.
He then descended from his seat. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "The Ultimate Way is without difficulty; it only dislikes discrimination.

He held up his staff and said, "Baoning’s staff has already pierced through the nostrils of all the patch-robed monks in the world at once. He struck the ground with it once and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Dharma-body is formless, yet it manifests forms in response to things. Prajñā is without cognition, yet it illuminates in response to conditions.
Above is heaven; below is earth. The Buddha Hall faces the triple gate; the Sangha Hall faces the kitchen and storehouse. Holding up his staff, he said:
"This here is Baoning’s staff. Which one is the Dharma-body? If you can penetrate through this point, then for now..."
"In a village of three families, buying from the east and selling to the west—if one cannot penetrate through this, then even roaming freely across the world is not yet possible.
Jinling still has Fengtai Pass. *He strikes the meditation seat once and descends.*
Ascending the hall, he said: "It is vividly manifest within the space between mind and eye, yet its form cannot be seen. Holding up his staff, he asked, "Do you see it?
If you do see it, then how can one say its form cannot be seen? "It shines brilliantly within the realm of sensory objects, yet its principle cannot be divided."
He struck the staff and said, "Do you hear it yet? If you do, then how can one say it cannot be divided? To let go is easy; to grasp and gather is difficult.
Within a thicket of brambles, you must know there is a path for emerging. Try to offer a single phrase from within this state of 'seven times loose and eight times free.'* The assembly was silent.
He then said, "If you do not enter the water, how will you see the tall man? *Note: This refers to a state of total freedom and mastery in the Chan encounter dialogue.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Everyone says there is this black-lacquered thing; it is only that its application differs.
In your own capacity, it stands vertically through the three periods of time and extends horizontally throughout the ten directions, pointing to the great earth as pure gold."
Churning the great river into cream and butter—this resides within Baoning’s hands. If you want it horizontal, it will not be horizontal; if you want it vertical, it will not be vertical.
To touch it is to perish; to look at it is to go blind. At such a time, those who are frantic fill the heavens and cover the earth.
[Descend from the seat.]
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "A north wind blows across the great earth; Snowflakes fly through the long, vast sky. The cold is more intense this morning;

Add another layer of clothing upon your bodies. Great assembly, if you have clothes, then add them; if you have no clothes, what can you add? By the brazier, one still complains of the chill while warming oneself by the fire;
Yet there is the woodcutter who walks barefoot."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring rain is like fat; the spring wind is like a blade. It fills the ditches and blocks the ravines; it uproots trees and makes the branches whistle.
Do you understand? When the fish swim, the water becomes turbid; when the bird flies, its feathers fall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "It cannot be known by wisdom; it cannot be recognized by consciousness. Holding up his staff, he said, "O Assembly, what do you call this?
If you call it a staff, your eyebrows and whiskers will fall off. If you do not call it a staff, you will sink into the level ground.
Try to offer a single phrase from a place where not even a hair’s breadth is moved! After a long silence, he said: "At home, they simply say..."
It is easy for a guest; only when facing the fishing trap does one realize how difficult it is to catch the fish.

*Pats the meditation seat once.* Descends from the seat. Enters the hall. "Why such contrivance? Last night at the third watch, Master Bodhidharma struck down with a single punch the front tooth of Baoning.
Question: "I know you understand how to hold the starless scale; how much does the hornless iron ox weigh? Answer: [Silence] (or *Pats the meditation seat once*).
"The head is light and the tail is heavy. The monk said, "This is still face-to-face deception. He replied, "It serves as a model for all people under heaven.
The monk said, "If that is so, then when people are level they do not speak; when water is level it does not flow. He replied, "It is still somewhat lacking. [The monk] asked:
At Mount Ling, they point to the moon; at Caoxi, they paint the moon. I wonder, what is it like under the gate of Baoning? The Master said, "Ha!
The monk said, "A flower is right before one's face. The Master then gave a shout. The monk said, "Once the mandarin ducks are embroidered, let them be viewed as such;
do not pass the golden needle to others. He replied, "Rarely does one encounter a guest with pierced ears."
Chan Master Dajue arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "Like sounds respond to one another, and like breaths seek one another out.
When Dingguang beckons with his hand, Zhiyi nods his head. Although it is thus, it still cannot avoid making others' mouths laugh until they split."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The single, firm, and dense body manifests within all atoms. Therefore, in walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, every thought-moment is unborn;
in seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, every mind is eternally quiescent.
In a single thought-instant, the youth Sudhana passed through one hundred and ten cities and visited fifty-three spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), yet upon arrival, he did not depart from Bodhi."
At the site of enlightenment, in the Hall of Universal Radiance, Vairocana and Maitreya follow step by step; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra appear everywhere.
If you can see through this with true clarity, you must further know that there is a path leading upward before you have attained it.
Furthermore, as for the one path that points upward—how is it? *Hūṃ, hūṃ!* [The Master] descends from his seat. Ascending the hall:
In the gate of the Patriarchs, human tracks are severed; Its depth and peril exceed a ten-thousand-fathom pit.
If you lower your hand, you cannot avoid wasting your effort; Let the green moss grow upon the dais as it will.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma to provide for the assembly, one cannot avoid the falling out of eyebrows and whiskers.
If one speaks of worldly matters to provide for the assembly, one enters hell as swiftly as a flying arrow. Leaving these two paths aside, what should one say?
A three-inch tongue has no place to use; a pair of empty hands do not form a fist."
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and shouted, saying: "Do not toil in vain; cease your drudgery. The light of formlessness is ever before one’s eyes.
Take up your short oar and solitary boat and go home; the misty waves of the five lakes and four seas are sufficient. He threw down the staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The gateway of Baoning has long been open; robes-clad companions come and go in endless succession. Where lie the two waters and three mountains?
You must go there in person to reach the Phoenix Terrace."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The mechanism of 'biting the iron spike' is still dull; being struck at the point of the spearhead is not yet intimate.
When the ten-faced, thousand-eyed Nanda moves, the formless numinous light eclipses the sun's orb. He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
At Dapingzhou Ruizhu, the Master ascended the hall. The host had commanded him to ascend this seat to preach the Dharma for the assembly.
If one discusses this seat, there is nowhere to ascend, yet there is nowhere that is not ascended. If one discusses this Dharma, there is nothing to be said, yet there is nothing that is not said.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time were also like this; the patriarchs of the East and West were also like this; and all people here are also like this.
Baoning was also like this. Since it is thus, who is the one sitting? Who is the one standing? Who is the one speaking?
Who is the one listening? If you understand this, it is already placing a head upon a head;
if you do not understand, let it be—go ahead and cut off your own head to seek life.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Brahma-realms of the ten directions are as one family. Assigning duties according to talent is like buying a hat to fit the head.
For us monks, twice every day upon our long benches, we open our mats, unfold our bowls, pick up the spoons, and grasp the chopsticks—what is lacking here?
Dough cakes, noodles, sugar cakes, and dumplings are but ordinary fare. Even so, nevertheless..."
The Way: the handle of the ladle is in Master Shi’s hand. If you understand this, you may eat and drink as you please;
if you do not, today we have newly appointed a new head cook.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "The notes gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu; metal, wood, water, fire, and earth.
He struck the floor once and said, "The auspicious and inauspicious are distinguished upon the hexagrams. Look for them three days from now."

Ascending the hall, Baoning said: "In my ordinary dealings with people, I point directly to that which is faceless. If one were to strike the bone to extract the marrow, it would truly cause the gods to wail and the ghosts to weep.
Clapping his hands, he laughed and said: "Benevolence and righteousness are both severed where there is nothing;
worldly sentiments lean toward those who have wealth."
Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally across his body and said, "You great men of character must cut through things with a single stroke, leaving no two ends;
you must act directly, moving freely in all directions. He then cast the staff down and said, "Wait, let the people of the world pass judgment."
Question: “The cold wind withers the fallen leaves; one still rejoices that an old friend has returned. I wonder, who is this ‘old friend’?
Answer: “Yangqi passed away long ago. The monk said: “Is there anyone else who understands this? Answer: “The sightless village elder nods his head in the dark.
The monk said: “Does the dead firewood have smoke or flame? There is surely no one who knows it alone. Answer: “Today.”

The furnace had not yet been opened. A monk asked, "What if one suddenly encounters a time when things are flowing freely in all directions? The Master replied, "It would be better to withdraw your hand.
The monk said, "Who knows that within the mist and haze there is still a fisherman? The Master replied, "Do not speak so recklessly."
The Master and Li Taibo recited the verse on the three phrases. Taibo said, "This is simply an unresolved case.
The Master said, "Please try to judge it for me. Taibo said, "Eight blows, thirteen [blows].
The Master said, "What fault does Baoning have? Taibo was speechless. The Master said, "Precisely, this is an unresolved case."
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following]: "Night after night, one embraces the Buddha in sleep; morning after morning, one rises together with him.
Rising and sitting, we are always in each other’s company; speaking and remaining silent, we dwell together. Not separated by so much as a hair’s breadth, they are like a body and its shadow.

If you wish to know where the Buddha goes, it is simply this sound of my voice. "Great Assembly, this verse by Master Fu has not fallen into ruin since antiquity; everyone knows it. Regarding this..."
There are many who have caught a glimpse [of the truth], yet few who have not misunderstood it. Xuansha said, "The Great Master Fu Daoshi recognized nothing more than this 'bright and alert' state.
Dongshan Cong said, "Tell me, does a patch-robed monk ever sleep during the day?
Regarding these two turns of phrase: "Who says there are no immortals in the world? One must believe that within the alchemical elixir jar there is another heaven."
Baoning also had one verse: When it is time to sleep, I sleep; when it is time to rise, I rise. Washing my face, my skin is radiant;
sipping tea, my beak is moistened. Red dust arises in the great ocean; waves surge upon level ground. Hehe! Ahehe! Lalili! Lalili!
[The assembly] descended from their seats.
Ascending the hall. When the assembly had gathered and settled, he remained silent for a long while and said, "What can one possibly do? Then he descended from his seat. Ascending the hall.
When the assembly had gathered and settled, he remained silent for a long while and said, "It is still somewhat lacking. Then he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Look, look! This mountain monk is entering the Hell of the Plucked Tongue. With his hand, he pulled out his tongue and cried, "A-ya! A-ya!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad phenomena of the universe all appear within this mirror. Pointing with his staff, he said: "To the north is the kitchen and storehouse;
to the south is the Sangha Hall; in the middle is the Buddha Hall. Then, pointing directly downward, he asked: "What is this?"
He then said: "You do not even recognize this footstool.
Question: "What is the realm of Baoning? Answer: "The main mountain peak stands upside down. Follow-up: "What is the person within the realm?
Answer: "One nostril is missing. Question: "What is the house style of Baoning? Answer: "Hard *hūbǐng* (glutinous rice cakes) and soft *lànbǐng* (steamed cakes)."
[The Master] was eating noodles. [A monk] stepped forward and said, "If a guest were to arrive suddenly, with what would you receive them? He replied, "Coarse food satisfies easily;
fine chewing does not lead to hunger. [The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "One is unaware of the stench of one's own excrement."
Ascending the hall, he said: "One is one; two is two; three is three; four is four. The numbers are very clear.
Superiors and subordinates follow the order of seniority. Following the order of seniority—what business is there? [He] drew a line with his staff and said:
"O Assembly, you have all thrown the sixty-year sexagenary cycle into total confusion at once!"
Ascending the hall: when walking, walk; when standing, stand; when sitting, sit; when lying down, lie down. Raising your hands and taking your steps are all free and easy.
Where and when could there ever be a lapse? Carve out your own belly yourself;
eat your rice and gruel, and do not endure hunger. A-he-he! Do you remember? This year, the eleventh month is small, and the twelfth month is large.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "When Śākyamuni was first born, he walked seven steps and gazed in the four directions.
At such a time, the land was vast and people were few; those who encountered him were rare. He then pointed with his hand toward heaven and earth—right there in a village of three households."
Divining east, divining west, he then said: "In all the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. Since the ancestors did not resolve this, the calamity has reached their descendants.
Stepping down from his seat, he leaned his hand against the meditation platform and called to the assembly: "Thirty years hence, you must not misrepresent this!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The mute sings; the deaf clap their hands. Through the eternal night, the wind is clear and the moon is a vacant white.
A scorched brick strikes the frozen ground through to its very bottom. At dawn, a single orb of light blazes forth. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are drunk and know not of it.
The people of Bohai and Silla all gaze upward with bared foreheads. Aha! Aha! What is this? Let them sit in a pit of excrement; let them lie in deep grass. He struck the water.

The long boat is high; the mud is deep, the Buddha is great. When the public case (kung-an) manifests before you, comprehend it all at once. He drew a line with his staff and descended from the seat. Entering the hall:

"That which belonged to the ancients is used by those of today; that which belongs to those of today was practiced by the ancients. There is no distinction between front and back throughout past and present."
How few people of old knew this? Ye-woo-i. One-nine and two-nine, meeting yet not extending a hand.
Entering the hall: A seedless sprout grows in the midst of fire; iron flowers bloom upon the treetops. Suddenly, a round fruit is formed;
when shown to people of the present age, they find it within themselves.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The realms of boundless lands are not separated from one another by so much as a hair’s tip; the ten ages of past and present do not depart from this very moment of thought.
Vertically, they exhaust the three periods of time; horizontally, they pervade the ten directions. Principle and phenomena are perfectly interfused; essence and appearance are equal."
Palaces and towers are adorned everywhere; grasses, trees, mountains, and rivers manifest in successive layers. As bells ring and drums resound, they perpetually proclaim the sound of liberation.
In every word and phrase of written and spoken language, the principle of *tathatā* (suchness) is fully revealed.
Free from "that" and "this," beyond right and wrong, the inclusion of Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed is not considered extraordinary; it is like the myriad rivers returning to the great ocean.
This is simply the ordinary state, wherein all distinctions between great and small have utterly vanished, and the marks of existence and non-existence are no longer perceived.

Therefore, manifestation and concealment are sovereign, and going and staying are without fixed direction. Abiding among the mundane, one is not mundane; dwelling with the sages, one is not a sage. This is the inconceivable realm.
People are constantly within it, yet for what reason do they not realize it themselves?
